# XY Forever serial protocol 1.31: boot and device commands

Part of the [XY Forever serial protocol 1.31](../PROTOCOL.md).

### 0x20 `boot.install`

Install the staged XY Forever build into the boot partition. Accepts only a staged XY Forever build (its cold descriptor and a valid LDR structure; `image`
otherwise) that fits the boot partition (`too_large`). Writes with the stock bootloader's own A/B boot-partition writer, then reads the partition back and
compares every byte (`install` on any difference). Sends `log` events while it runs. A wrong-length request or no complete staging is `state`. Once the writer
has run (`ok` or `install`) the staging is used up; a request refused before writing leaves it as it was. Takes minutes; the host waits up to 900 s.

| Request field (32 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again |

| Reply field, after the status (12 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `written` | u32 | non-zero when the boot-partition writer finished |
| `partition` | u32 | active boot partition read back (1 or 2; 0 = none) |
| `sectors` | u32 | 512-byte sectors read back and compared |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `state`, `sha`, `image`, `link`, `too_large`, `install`. Tool timeout: 900 s. **Destructive**: ask
the user first. Since 1.0.

### 0x21 `boot.uninstall`

Put the stock 1.2.1 os.ldr back into the boot partition. As `boot.install`, but accepts only the exact stock OP-XY 1.2.1 `os.ldr` (2373336 bytes, SHA-256
`60358afdaa9b58ed40411602f6d5d4e1e3e02553ff2da7e25038e71dd002b52f`). From 1.26, both boot writers return to the ordinary file service after selecting user
storage, allowing the host to restore the root OS file and clean up while XY Forever still runs. `boot.uninstall` itself leaves the files under
`/yaffs2/xy-forever/` in place. The next restart boots stock 1.2.1.

| Request field (32 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again |

| Reply field, after the status (12 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `written` | u32 | non-zero when the boot-partition writer finished |
| `partition` | u32 | active boot partition read back (1 or 2; 0 = none) |
| `sectors` | u32 | 512-byte sectors read back and compared |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `state`, `sha`, `image`, `link`, `too_large`, `install`. Tool timeout: 900 s. **Destructive**: ask
the user first. Since 1.0.

### 0x30 `device.reboot`

Restart both processors. The reply comes first; the device restarts about 50 ms later and the USB port goes away. Wait for the port to come back, then send
`hello`. Targets 0 and 2 behave the same today. A target above 2 is `bad_request`; a payload that is neither empty nor 4 bytes counts as no target.

| Request field (0 to 4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | u32 | Optional. 0 = the XY Forever menu with USB; 1 = the default firmware (OS); 2 = the XY Forever menu with USB. Where the device goes; without it: 2 |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x31 `menu.continue`

Leave the menu and boot the default firmware. After the ok reply the menu closes and USB goes away. Any other payload, or a mode above 1, is answered with
`link` (not `bad_request`); so is a dry run processor A did not accept. Modes 2 and 3 ("open the menu with USB", outside boot model v3) are not part of v1: the
menu is the home loop that answers this protocol, so a tool that is connected is already in the menu.

| Request field (0 to 4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | u32 | Optional. 0 = boot the default firmware; 1 = dry run: the whole boot path without starting the OS, then back to the menu. Without it: 0 |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `link`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x32 `service.hold`

Keep the device in the menu across restarts.

| Request field (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `on` | u32 | 0 = off; 1 = on. On: stay in the XY Forever menu (with USB) across `device.reboot` until power-off |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x35 `menu.converge`

Converge, then boot: the saved inputs, or one library entry once; and the sequence's state. Modes 1 and 2 answer at once with the state after the start (1); the
menu then runs the sequence on its progress screen and USB stays up, so `job.status` follows each job (a build, a content switch, the record, the fingerprint)
and mode 0 says how it stands. When it boots, the menu closes and USB goes away; when it ends without booting, the menu stays, shows why, and mode 0 answers
state 2 with that reason. Mode 1 is the first row's Continue: the converge before every boot (docs/storage/state.md). Mode 2 boots a library entry once, as
`library.boot`, but installs its content first (always: an entry rebuilt into the same slot keeps its id; before it, when the stock base has no content set, as
on an OP-XY that never saved mods, the content-set job makes it, #284), and changes nothing saved: the next plain power-on finds the default's content missing
and converges back to the saved inputs (xyf dev, #204). `busy` while a sequence or a job runs, and for mode 2 while a content journal is open (the menu replays
it first); `not_found`, no such entry; `state`, it has no `os.ldr`; `link`, processor A does not serve.

| Request field (41 to 72 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | u32 | API version: 1; newer is unsupported |
| `mode` | u32 | 0 = report the sequence's state only; 1 = converge to the saved inputs, then boot the default (as PLAY on the menu's first row); 2 = boot library entry `id` once with its own content: its content switch, then the boot; the saved inputs, the default and the fingerprint stay. What to do |
| `id` | cstr ASCII, 1..32 B | mode 2: the library entry id (1-31 of `a-z 0-9 _ -`); empty for modes 0 and 1 |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of every request byte before it |

| Reply field, after the status (12 to 92 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | u32 | reply format: 1 |
| `state` | u32 | 0 = idle: no sequence runs (the last one, if any, booted or ended with a note); 1 = running on the menu's progress screen; 2 = the last sequence ended without booting: `reason`; 3 = booting: the menu closes on its next pass and USB goes away. The converge sequence (a plain power-on's too) |
| `job` | u32 | the job running now, or the last one (0: none this boot): follow it with `job.status` |
| `reason` | text ASCII, 0..80 B | with state 2: why, as the menu's status line says it; else empty |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `unsupported`, `sha`, `busy`, `link`, `not_found`, `state`. The reply never gains fields (it ends in
`text`). Tool timeout: 30 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since
1.31.
